logline: Four elite families living in a gated Seoul enclave compete to get their children into SKY universities - a dark comedy about the violence ambition inflicts on people who believe they deserve to win.

renewal.note: Single-season series; concluded February 2019. Became the highest-rated Korean cable drama in history at time of broadcast (23.8% finale).

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.5; 23.8% finale rating - the highest in Korean cable history at the time; won four Baeksang Awards; critics praised the show's combination of satirical precision and genuine psychological horror in how it depicts elite parental obsession.

pull_quotes.text: A razor-sharp satire of Korean educational anxiety that keeps escalating into something genuinely terrifying.

seasons.review_body: SKY Castle started as a dark comedy about college admissions and ended as a psychological thriller about the cost of ambition - the genre shift is not a flaw but the show's central structural argument. The 23.8% finale rating remains one of the benchmarks of Korean cable television history. Critics identified Kim Seo-hyung's Kim Joo-young - the tutor coordinator who manages the families' university ambitions - as one of the great antagonists in recent Korean drama: frightening precisely because she is entirely rational. The show's satire of Korea's educational hierarchy landed as both entertainment and genuine social commentary; it aired during a period when the SKY university system was a live national conversation. Won four Baeksang Arts Awards including Best Drama. The 20-episode run is tight - extended to satisfy demand, but not a frame of it is indulgent.

episode_reviews.title: Pilot
episode_reviews.review_body: SKY Castle Season 1 Episode 1 aired November 23, 2018 on JTBC as the premiere of the 20-episode series. IMDb audience scored the season 8.5; the finale drew a 23.8% cable rating - the highest in Korean cable television history at the time. SKY Castle won four Baeksang Arts Awards including Best Drama. The Rotten Tomatoes consensus called it 'a razor-sharp satire of Korean educational anxiety that keeps escalating into something genuinely terrifying.' The premiere establishes the enclave's hierarchy with satirical precision - house size, school performance, and the invisible currency of implied wealth are mapped in the first act. The tone is pitch-black comedy until the final scene, where the show signals it intends to go somewhere darker. Kim Seo-hyung's tutor coordinator appears briefly and the temperature drops in the way that announces a particular kind of antagonist.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The opening episode establishes the enclave's hierarchy with scalpel precision - who lives in the biggest house, who hides their scholarship, who performs confidence while drowning in debt. The tone is pitch-black comedy until the final scene, which pivots to something considerably colder.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final image of the pilot announces that this show is not interested in satire that stays at arm's length.

critic_note.text: A drama that knows exactly what it wants to be from minute one.

episode_reviews.title: The Tutor's Past
episode_reviews.review_body: SKY Castle Season 1 Episode 16 'The Tutor's Past' aired January 18, 2019 on JTBC. IMDb audience scored the series 8.5; the finale reached 23.8% cable - the highest in Korean cable history at the time. The Rotten Tomatoes consensus called it 'a razor-sharp satire that keeps escalating into something genuinely terrifying.' The sixteenth episode is the season's structural pivot - the information it reveals about Kim Joo-young retroactively reframes every scene she appeared in across the preceding fifteen episodes. Kim Seo-hyung performs the revelation with the precision of an actor who has known the character's full history since the first day of shooting: nothing in her earlier work contradicts this disclosure, and everything in it becomes suddenly, retrospectively legible. Critics consistently cited this as the episode where SKY Castle confirmed it was operating in a different genre from the dark comedy it appeared to be.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode that recontextualises everything. The show's most controlled piece of sustained tension - information withheld until the precise moment it lands with maximum impact. Kim Seo-hyung does career-best work here. Critics cited this as the point where SKY Castle stops being a drama about education and reveals itself as something darker entirely.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Kim Joo-young's history surfaces and changes the grammar of every scene she has appeared in before it.

critic_note.text: The episode that confirms SKY Castle is playing in a different league.
